:::{#thm-projection-matrix-projects}
#### A projection matrix projects onto its column space, and is the only one that does

1. If $\matr{P}$ is a $p \times p$ orthogonal projection matrix (@def-projection-matrix),
   then for every $\vecf{y} \in \reals^p$,
   $\matr{P} \vecf{y}$ is the orthogonal projection of $\vecf{y}$ onto $\mathcal{C}(\matr{P})$
   (@def-orthogonal-projection).
2. If $\matr{P}_1$ and $\matr{P}_2$ are $p \times p$ matrices
   such that, for every $\vecf{y}$,
   both $\matr{P}_1 \vecf{y}$ and $\matr{P}_2 \vecf{y}$
   are the orthogonal projection of $\vecf{y}$ onto the same subspace $\mathcal{S}$,
   then $\matr{P}_1 = \matr{P}_2$.

:::

::: proof

**Part 1.**
Write $\vecf{y} = \matr{P} \vecf{y} + (\vecf{y} - \matr{P} \vecf{y})$.
The first term is in $\mathcal{C}(\matr{P})$ (@def-column-space).
For the second,

$$
\ba
\matr{P}\,(\vecf{y} - \matr{P} \vecf{y})
&= \matr{P} \vecf{y} - \matr{P}\,(\matr{P} \vecf{y})
&& \text{(@thm-matvec-linear, with coefficients } 1 \text{ and } -1 \text{)}
\\
&= \matr{P} \vecf{y} - (\matr{P} \matr{P})\,\vecf{y}
&& \text{(@thm-matmul-assoc)}
\\
&= \matr{P} \vecf{y} - \matr{P}^2 \vecf{y}
&& \text{(@def-matrix-power)}
\\
&= \matr{P} \vecf{y} - \matr{P} \vecf{y}
&& \text{(} \matr{P} \text{ is idempotent)}
\\
&= \vzero_p,
&& \text{(arithmetic)}
\ea
$$

so $\vecf{y} - \matr{P} \vecf{y} \in \mathcal{N}(\matr{P})$.
Since $\matr{P} = \tp{\matr{P}}$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal{N}(\matr{P}) &= \mathcal{N}(\tp{\matr{P}}) \\
&= \mathcal{C}(\matr{P})^\perp
\end{aligned}
$$

(@thm-complement-null-space).
By the uniqueness in @thm-orthogonal-direct-sum,
$\matr{P} \vecf{y}$ is the orthogonal projection of $\vecf{y}$ onto $\mathcal{C}(\matr{P})$.

**Part 2.**
The orthogonal projection of a vector onto $\mathcal{S}$ is unique (@def-orthogonal-projection),
so $\matr{P}_1 \vecf{e}_j = \matr{P}_2 \vecf{e}_j$
for each indicator vector $\vecf{e}_j$ (@def-indicator-vector).
$\matr{P}_1 \vecf{e}_j$ is column $j$ of $\matr{P}_1$:
by @thm-matvec-columns it is the combination of the columns of $\matr{P}_1$
with coefficients the entries of $\vecf{e}_j$,
which are $1$ in place $j$ and $0$ elsewhere (@def-indicator-vector).
Likewise for $\matr{P}_2$,
so the two matrices have the same columns.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-projection-matrix-projects}
#### Two routes to the same projection matrix

The matrix $\matr{P} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$
of @exm-projection-matrix is an orthogonal projection matrix,
and its column space is $\operatorname{span}\cb{(1, 0)}$, the horizontal axis.
By part 1, $\matr{P}(v_1, v_2) = (v_1, 0)$ is the orthogonal projection onto that axis:
the remainder $(0, v_2)$ is orthogonal to $(1, 0)$.
The vector $\vecf{q}_1 = (1, 0)$ has length $1$ and spans the axis,
so it is an orthonormal basis of it, and with $\matr{B} = [\vecf{q}_1]$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\matr{B} \tp{\matr{B}} &= \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix} \\
&= \matr{P},
\end{aligned}
$$

as part 2 and @thm-projector-onb require.

The oblique projection $\matr{Q} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$
of @exm-projection-matrix also maps every vector into the horizontal axis.
It sends $(0, 1)$ to $(1, 0)$,
but the remainder $(0, 1) - (1, 0) = (-1, 1)$ is not orthogonal to the axis,
so $(1, 0)$ is not the orthogonal projection of $(0, 1)$ onto the axis,
which is $\matr{P}(0, 1) = (0, 0)$.

:::
